paras: Hospital OPD software manages the outpatient side of a hospital: registering or finding the patient, booking an appointment or issuing a walk-in token, queuing them to the right doctor, recording the consultation, sending the prescription to the pharmacy and raising the OPD bill. HIMS does all of this as one flow on one patient record.

The OPD dashboard is the front desk's screen for the morning. It shows appointments due, walk-ins registered, how many patients are waiting, and the live queue outside each consulting room. Because the same record continues into the laboratory, imaging and IP admission, an OP visit that turns into an admission does not start again from a blank form.

sections.h2: The OPD is where the hospital is judged, and where paper slows it most.
sections.lead: Patients form their opinion of the hospital in the first forty minutes. Most of that time is spent waiting for a process, not a doctor.

items.p: A returning patient gives their name, age and address again because nobody can find the old file.
The booked patient and the walk-in argue at the door because there is no single order for the doctor's queue.

items.h: The doctor cannot see the queue
items.p: The consultant asks the attender how many are waiting; the attender counts heads in the corridor.
The paper prescription is lost between the consulting room and the pharmacy counter, and the patient comes back to the doctor.
The doctor says come back in two weeks; there is no booking, so nobody knows whether the patient returned.

items.q: Does the OPD software handle both appointments and walk-ins?
items.a: Yes. Appointments are booked by doctor and slot, walk-ins receive a token at the desk, and both feed the same live queue for the doctor. The OPD dashboard shows appointments, walk-ins and the waiting count together.

items.q: Can the doctor see the queue from the consulting room?
items.a: Yes. Each doctor has a live queue in HIMS, so the consultant sees who is next and how many are waiting without asking an attender to count.

items.q: Is OPD billing part of the same system?
items.a: Yes. Consultation and procedure charges are pulled from the visit into the bill, with cash, insurance and TPA handled in one billing view and GST applied where it applies. See hospital billing software.
HIMS includes a patient app and portal through which patients can book appointments and view their reports. Walk-ins are still registered at the desk in the usual way.

items.q: What happens when an OP patient needs admission?
items.a: The visit is converted into an IP admission on the same record. Bed allocation, orders, nursing and IP billing continue from there. See IPD software.

items.q: Can I see it working before a call?
items.a: Yes. The hospital demo opens the OPD dashboard with sample data, and the live environment at his.elevateaura.co.in shows the same screens your front desk would use.
